units.reason: Flying into Charon, Sker, Tethys, Pallas, or Dione charts the activity hull there and speaks its scan line.
Spore catalyst and gate handshakes show as living samples and lattice credentials instead of ordinary freight.
Asking at Research Station Veil names Page Nine, and Ashfall names the Charon garden while Big Ballast is off the lane.
A hold of spore catalyst or a live specimen reads as Concord risk, Frontier wary, and Quiet favor instead of a blank conscience.
A hard hit cracks spore catalyst and the unbroken lens into scoopable spill, and leaves iron ore and a gate handshake in the hold.
Dumping spore catalyst, a live specimen, or filament leaves a green pod that eats hull on contact, and ore stays inert.
Fauna in the Veil null corridor scatter where the pocket actually sits, including far from the sector origin.
The Veil containment core stays alive; only the seal ring around it scatters fauna.
A broken directive and a revoked route name themselves on the scanner instead of looking like strangers.
An exception grant renames the machine as route authority on file, not as a witnessed contact.
The Veil revoked gate says the route is closed, and flying out does not count as obeying.
A witness mark stays on file, but a fault makes the Veil gate auditor ask again.
The first Charon pylon sighting announces the observed scan label, not a compliance grade you have not earned.
When a claim fight falls apart, the yard says the raid is still coming and how long you have to get back.
A loss headline names the house that lost the hull, including Helix and the Archive, and an unknown house is no longer called A a ship.
Shooting a bounty hunter while the jump spool is winding tells you the spool was interrupted.
In an Io Reach fight, the director still calls it a fight after a long quiet log.
A fight queued at Sker does not count as combat waiting for you at Helios.
Helios's sector report names the Memorial Array anomaly instead of saying the hazards are clear.
The open Veil to Ashfall wormhole plots as one gate hop, not a long drift.
When Ceres and Io cost the same fuel, the route goes through the quieter Tethys junction.
When two tar clouds overlap, the escape cue points at the one you are deepest in.
Your reserved pad at Helios stays yours when the next ship arrives.
A hauler still in the Helios yard after midnight stays on the board.
Scanning the veil rays at Quiet Ice makes them flinch and keep fleeing.
Gunfire breaks the needle swarm's ring and they run, while a veil ray nearby stays put.
An archive crab builds a debris pile you can read, and the pile falls when the crab dies.
A wake eel's trail pulls a cold furnace maw in, and the maw charges.
Towing a suture mite off its seam and letting go leaves it defensive.
When a stone lung exhales, nearby grazers break off and feed on the plume.
Glassbacks read as scattered glass until you get close, and the stone lung beside them keeps its name.
Close to a cold bell, it names itself and tolls before the radiation front.
Recovering the Cinder Nursery recorder does not wipe a fault already on your standing.
Veil step stops in front of a solid wreck instead of dropping the hull inside it.
Docking at the den with hot cargo and not enough credits now says the cut and leaves the pod hot.
The salvage cradle says Stellarite Ore when that core lands in the bay, instead of the raw ore id.
Clearing a loaded lane names the ore you would lose and waits for a second confirm.
Pouring a fuel cell into a tank that cannot take it now says how much room is left, and a booked pump says it already owns the gap.
A core in a hollow hall cuts its output from heat, the claim says so on the first watch, and the board no longer calls that machine idle.
A drone whose hold is full hails Reach Station by name instead of calling a named berth a depot.
A cradle set into a full salvage bay keeps the core and the units that did not fit, and finishes them once the bay has room.

Entering Charon Expanse, Sker Haven or Tethys Junction has the dock speak the garden hull, ballast barge or Re-router rumor and chart its bearing — and the unique-wreck census now stays green over all 22 authored hulls.

The six open factions — Understory, Fulfillment, Archive, Pitborn, Free Frontier, Verge-Layers — now have canon sketches in the canonical factions file, each marked PROVISIONAL (R10, 2026-10-21), so the story bible the narrative lane writes from finally matches the fourteen factions the game fields.
Breaking an enemy part names that part. Your own ship still uses the long sentences.
Hours 11-15 of the research ladder are authored verbs from existing late nodes. Seeds 4242 and 15510 see the same rows.
A latch whose open segment crosses a live wreck or station hull is refused, and a sidestep that clears the hull opens the line.
A ship wrecked by the player's thrown mass says so. An NPC-on-NPC crash keeps the old line.
Thrown mass on a swarm champion tears a rotating capital part. Mission fights stay on the same rotation.
Recipes that fire in the first hour caption as authored sentences. None fall through to an id-built line.
Incoming telegraph, repulsor deployed, and massline captions are in the source inventory a translation pass can read.
A telegraph from 8 o'clock captions as 8 o'clock, using the same position that pans the cue.
A committed jump, an arrival, and an interdiction each emit one caption. Repeats inside the dedupe window stay one.
A crushing massline hit reads heavier than a solid hit, and a glance is the lightest, on the existing impact lane.
A kill by another ship does not file as your Kill clip. A kill you make still does.
Your death files one Death clip. A hit that does not kill you files none.
Only capital weapons opens in that stretch, once, at hour 12.31. Stamping earlier and later doors as hours 11-15 made the research screen lie. Those labels are off.

units.reason: A captain link for a roster id names the captain, their home station, and one thing already lived with them.
A passenger liner with a settled last leg shows arrived, returned, or lost, plus the station. An unset leg shows nothing.
After an automated asset is lost, the automation desk keeps kind, sector, and value from the existing loss log.
Contract history reads First contracts, Working spacer, Established, or Veteran. A new pilot reads First contracts.
Two board jobs wait for rank steps 2 and 3. A step-1 pilot is told the rank title they still need.
Allied standing posts one Drift haul a trusted pilot cannot take, and that rung can read as reached.
Dock notices are 353. Every faction and station type has a sponsor, and sectors name local businesses.
Wall tags are 365, keyed by sector and faction, including cast and landmarks, with none about the player.
Understory, Fulfillment, Archive, Pitborn, Verge-Layers, and Free Frontier each have at least four tags, and each motto is the bible line.
Every station type can name a hull that is actually in the sector. The line does not address the player.
At least six partner errands get a reply from the other hull. Two speakers, no player address.
Toll, scan, queue, and hostile gates each have at least six lines. The scene picker is unchanged.
At least six errands name a second live hull and whether it is loaded, disabled, or fleeing.
The share-heat choice stays shut until a heat lure is fitted, and a commodity gate stays shut until the hold has it.
Each spawned squad gets a faction callsign. Two squads on the same seed do not share one.
Tethys time trial shows three medal times. A run under silver stores silver and survives save.
The racing ghost draws its own Quarry Hook. Older ghost tapes still play.
Shoving Rook into the shutter costs him two seconds and posts a receipt. His own crash does not.
Mira anchors the Quarry Hook on at least two of three laps. The other rivals do not.
At chain cap the guns fire about three times as fast until the chain breaks. It is not always on.
The foundry offers at least ten trades. Each spends two or more held parts and lands one existing module.
The first free flight shows one control card with the keys you actually use, once per profile.
The first cargo into an empty hold names the manifest key once. Later cargo stays quiet.
The first cross-sector route names Engage on the Star Map once and does not fly the route.
Speed still shows WU/S and also says world units per second. Distance on that HUD says world units.
The first wanted mark says what it is and that it clears over time or distance, once.
The first autosave says Progress saved. Later saves do not.
Title mode verbs (Crucible, Archive, Circuits, Sandbox, Physics challenges) show a visible one-line gloss instead of aria-only labels
Starter pick's Line stat shows a visible measure gloss ('massline winch speed') on both the arc cells and the hull ring
The contracts board says how many of three runs are done before a regular client pins.
A rescued captain's offer names the run number once the live cycle is two or more.
Tow, bulk, and salvage contracts can each earn a regular desk client.
From the third cycle the relief run changes exactly one of goods, pay, or destination.
A regular desk client has a display name. The desk id string is unchanged.
Each station destination tile shows the help line it already had.
The first Accept says hold even when no collateral is at risk. The hold time is unchanged.
A Circuit round ends when the last rooted hive node dies, even if other hostiles remain.
A Circuit round ends when a fixed zone's clock fills. Leaving drains it. Kills do not finish it.
A Circuit round ends when the last core is collected. The glass shows found of total. Cores pay no credits.
A Circuit round ends when the named commander dies. The pack can still be flying. The kill word names them.
A Circuit round ends after the ship holds the fixed gate at the arena edge for about three seconds.
An elite or challenge room raises pack pressure and the purse. The ordinary room stays a choice. Ship stats and the Threat wager are untouched.
First-hour taught verbs (thrust/latch/fire/scan/beam) now print their live bound key on the rail line and the HUD objective
Winch tutorial line names hold + both reel axis ends with live bound labels
A capital torpedo can be latched and thrown by the Massline; the catch never defuses it
The tap-dash grants a 0.2 s damage-rejection window on the player hull only
Clips inside the tape but outside the recorded-sound window export video again instead of refusing
Game over bench carries a populated defeat state and an honest empty plate on separate seeds
LOG physics narrator carries 70 authored lines across all outcome kinds in the house filing register
A bought smart-bomb charge empties the room on one Bomb press: throw + packet, player untouched
The Orbital Lance call-in: telegraphed column strike on the aim point or the latched hull
An allied turret body fights beside you until the wave clears
Four allied escorts fly the wave and leave with it
A throwable lure pulls the pack off your tail and dies on its battery
The Shield Dome call-in plants a fixed external repulsor wall on a visible clock
A thrown body detonates on its first solid impact, credited to the player
Arena cover throws the pack back like a pinball table on a per-body cooldown
Every credited death ignites the bodies that stood close to it
The armory sells a stacking passive whose copies pile their effect on the run ledger, capped at five
chain_feeder legendary scales player damage packets +1pct per live chain point
echo legendary duplicates every fifth fitted player gun shot, deterministic per gun
Circuit wave three defends a beacon. The clock clears it alive. Losing it cuts the purse and the run continues.
Circuit wave fifteen escorts one unarmed freighter. Arrival clears the round. A loss cuts the purse and the run continues.
A route stop can open a derelict card. Salvage spends run credits and fits a part. Leave pays nothing. Either way the next stage fights.
